CEE Program Alumni Receive Davidson Fellows Scholarships

Image

McLean, Va. (September 29, 2026) – The Center for Excellence in Education (CEE) applauds CEE Research Science Institute (RSI) alumni who have been awarded Davidson Fellows Scholarships. 

Aditya Sengupta (RSI ’25) is a student at Bellevue High School, Washington. He has been awarded a $100,000 Davidson Fellows Scholarship for the science project, “ForeCAT: Advancing Clear Air Turbulence Prediction for Aviation Safety with Atmospheric Physics Informed Neural Networks and Spatiotemporal Weather Data.” He noted, “I enjoy crossing boundaries among physics, computer science and engineering and turning ideas into solutions that can work in the real world.” He is a Regeneron Science Talent Search Scholar and a National Junior Science and Humanities Symposium first place winner.

Pavan Subramani (RSI ’26) is a senior at Morgantown High School in West Virginia.  He has been awarded a $25,000 Davidson Fellows Scholarship for the science project, “The Hybridization of Generative Diffusion Models with Molecular Dynamics Simulations: A Novel Method to Accelerate Drug Discovery.” He noted, “I am interested in computational chemistry and biophysics and research that can advance human health through drug discovery.” He is a part-time Junior Fellow Director of the Harvard Undergraduate Microbiology Society. 

Honorable mentions included Eric Buehler from Madison, New Hampshire, and Annika Chadha from Prospect, Kentucky, both RSI ’26 alums.

“These students are building on their extraordinary RSI experience as scholars,” said Joann DiGennaro, CEE President. “They represent the future of U.S. global leadership in science and technology.” 

RSI is the most prestigious international summer research program in the world for high school students. Collaboratively sponsored with MIT, students conduct original, innovative research. CEE’s program emphasizes advanced theory and research in STEM. One hundred of the world’s most accomplished high school scholars are selected annually to participate in RSI, which is cost-free to all competitively selected students. To date, over 3,000 high school students representing every U.S. state and 63 nations have experienced RSI. For more information about RSI, visit https://www.cee.org/programs/research-science-institute.

 

###

About the Center for Excellence in Education

The Center for Excellence in Education (CEE), a nonprofit 501(c)(3) charitable organization, was founded in 1983 by the late Admiral H.G. Rickover and Joann P. DiGennaro, President of the Center. The Center’s mission is to nurture high school and university scholars to careers of excellence and leadership in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM), and to encourage collaboration between and among scientific and technological leaders in the global community. CEE sponsors the Research Science Institute (RSI), USA Biolympiad (USABO), Teacher Enrichment Program (TEP), and STEM Lyceums. CEE is a leading source for top STEM talent. For more information, visit https://www.cee.org.

About the Davidson Awards

The Davidson Fellows Scholarship awards annually recognize outstanding students 18 and under who have completed significant work in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) fields, music, and literature. The Davidson Fellows Scholarship has been named one of the most prestigious undergraduate scholarships by U.S. News & World Report.
